elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states that Customer “shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages” and negates the former 15%-of-annual-Fees weekly charge.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer shall not be liable for “any ... penalty.”

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer may arise only as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount at all. Because the condition for this fallback restriction—Customer owing a liquidated amount—is absent, no non-termination liquidated amount violates the requirement.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the rendered clause, so the conditional need for a three-month cap does not arise.

elements.element: The capped early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause makes no liquidated amount payable by Customer, so there is no additional or competing liquidated amount; the more protective preferred prohibition satisfies this fallback restriction.

result.reason: The operative revision eliminates the original late-payment liquidated-damages obligation and expressly disclaims both liquidated damages and penalties. It therefore fully meets the preferred position and, as the more protective result, also meets the fallback's conditional limits. The change is confined to the challenged remedy and does not disturb other payment obligations or remedies. Drafting quality is reduced because the obsolete trigger and 15%-per-week formula remain in a cumbersome negated sentence rather than being cleanly deleted.
